neighbours.label: joint action between the speaker or reader and a partner (together, we decide; you and your doctor can), versus the same task done by one party alone
fire: Our coach does not tell us what to do, but together, we plan each week of training.
You and your dentist can choose the right treatment for your sore tooth.
Read the first chapter together as a group before starting the quiz.
After the first meeting, together with your parents, we will build a study plan.
The couple sat down and together they worked out a monthly budget.
You and your manager should agree on clear goals for the new year.
Plant the seeds together with your children so they learn how gardens grow.
Our advisers listen first, and then together, we map out your retirement.
quiet: Our coach does not ask for opinions, and she plans each week of training herself.
Your dentist will choose the right treatment for your sore tooth.
Read the first chapter silently on your own before starting the quiz.
After the first meeting, our staff will send you a printed study plan.
The husband sat down and by himself he worked out a monthly budget.
Your manager will set clear goals for you for the new year.
Plant the seeds in rows about two inches apart so they grow well.
Our advisers review your file, and then they mail you a retirement report.

predictions: fire 0.25-0.6 on ' together' or the partner word in joint-action clauses; solo versions below 0.1
